```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(tibble)

# Run the analysis script that defines map_restaurants() and creates
# Run the geographic analysis script
source("scripts/geography_analysis.R")

required <- c("zip_result", "tracts_result", "neighborhood_result")
missing_results <- required[!vapply(required, exists, logical(1), inherits = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_results)) {
  stop("Missing result objects: ", paste(missing_results, collapse = ", "),
       ". Source your geographic analysis script in the setup chunk.")
}

results <- list(
  "ZIP/ZCTA" = zip_result,
  "Census tract" = tracts_result,
  "Neighborhood Statistical Area" = neighborhood_result
)
```

## Geographic coverage comparison

The table summarizes the geographic distribution of restaurants in the selected dietary-friendly categories: vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free.

It includes the number of geographic areas, unique restaurants assigned to an area, unmatched restaurants (including businesses with missing coordinates), and the minimum, median, and maximum number of restaurants per area. The minimum, median, and maximum are calculated using only areas with non-zero restaurant counts.

```{r comparison-table}
comparison_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(label) {
  result <- results[[label]]
  tibble(
    `Geographic system` = label,
    `Number of areas` = result$sample_size$total_areas,
    `Restaurants assigned` = result$coverage$matched,
    `Unmatched restaurants` = result$coverage$unmatched + result$coverage$missing_coordinates,
    `Areas with restaurants` = result$sample_size$total_areas - result$sample_size$empty_areas,
    `Min area count` = result$sample_size$min_restaurants,
    `Med area count` = result$sample_size$median_restaurants,
    `Max area count` = result$sample_size$max_restaurants
  )
}))

knitr::kable(comparison_table,
             caption = "Restaurant assignment and counts by geographic system")
```

## Restaurant counts by geographic area

All maps use the same longitude and latitude limits and the same color scale. Colors represent the number of restaurants assigned to each geographic area, not restaurant density per square kilometer.

```{r}
#| label: geographic-maps
#| column: screen
#| out-width: 90%
#| fig-cap: "Restaurant locations by geographic system, using a shared map extent."

make_map <- function(result, title) {
  ggplot() +
    # Geographic boundaries
    geom_sf(
      data = result$boundaries,
      fill = "grey95",
      color = "grey60",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ) +

    # Restaurant locations
    geom_sf(
      data = result$restaurants,
      color = "darkblue",
      alpha = 0.5,
      size = 0.7
    ) +

    # Same geographic extent for all maps
    coord_sf(
      xlim = c(-90.2, -90.0),
      ylim = c(29.9, 30.05),
      default_crs = st_crs(4326),
      expand = FALSE
    ) +

    labs(title = title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
    )
}

maps <- Map(make_map, results, names(results))

wrap_plots(maps, ncol = 3)
```

## Interpretation

```{r interpretation, results='asis'}
most_assigned <- comparison_table$`Geographic system`[
  which.max(comparison_table$`Restaurants assigned`)]
cat("The geographic system assigning the largest number of restaurants is **",
    most_assigned, "**. ", sep = "")

```
